The '''1982–83 Bundesliga''' was the 20th season of the [[Bundesliga]], [[West Germany]]'s premier football league. It began on 17 August 1982<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=327047 |title=Schedule Round 2 |publisher=DFB |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608084507/https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=327047 |archive-date=8 June 2011 }}</ref> and ended on 4 June 1983.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/competition/co12/se2604/all-matches/ |title=Bundesliga 1982/1983 » Schedule |website=WorldFootball.net |access-date=13 June 2020}}</ref> [[Hamburger SV]] were the defending champions.

==Competition modus==
Every team played two games against each other team, one at home and one away. Teams received two points for a win and one point for a draw. If two or more teams were tied on points, places were determined by [[goal difference]] and, if still tied, by goals scored. The team with the most points were crowned champions while the two teams with the fewest points were relegated to [[2. Bundesliga]]. The third-to-last team had to compete in a two-legged relegation/promotion play-off against the third-placed team from 2. Bundesliga.

==Team changes to 1981–82==
[[SV Darmstadt 98]] and [[MSV Duisburg]] were directly relegated to the [[1982–83 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]] after finishing in the last two places. They were replaced by [[FC Schalke 04]] and [[Hertha BSC]]. Relegation/promotion play-off participant [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen]] won on aggregate against [[Kickers Offenbach]] and thus retained their Bundesliga status.

==Relegation play-offs==
[[FC Schalke 04]] and third-placed [[1982–83 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]] team [[KFC Uerdingen 05|Bayer 05 Uerdingen]] had to compete in a two-legged relegation/promotion play-off. Uerdingen won 4–2 on aggregate and thus were promoted to the Bundesliga.
